<!--
THIS IS FIGURE 4---FIGURE SUPPLEMENT 1, settled 2026-08-11, declared at 04_results.tex in the
Figure~\ref{fig:plane} float. It took the declaration the line version had held. The file name
still carries the content rather than the number, and the deposit pass renames it. Ones written
against the superseded figure are parked in `../in_progress/figure_4_supplements_20260731/`.

WHAT IT IS. Figure 4's second moment, factored. Same plane, same rows, same members, same scale,
same two line families, same everything: the only thing that changes is what the top bar says.
Where Figure 4 nests moment > member > parameter, this nests COMPONENT > member > parameter, so a
reader who has paid for Figure 4 reads this one with no new instructions. 20 columns, the same as
the body figure, so the cell WIDTH is the body figure's; `per_row` is not shared, because it sets
the cell height against a different summed noise span. See the render chunk.

THE TWO COMPONENTS. The Gaussian information distortion factors into two congruences that the
battery computes separately:

  PER-SAMPLE     G^-1/2 J_sample G^-1/2, the departure of a SINGLE interval from the Gaussian the
                 algorithm assumes: the skewness and kurtosis of the one-step residual. It is
                 the price of the closure, and it must go to 1 as the channel count grows, since
                 that is when the binomial occupancy becomes normal.
  CORRELATION    J_sample^-1/2 J J_sample^-1/2, the temporal memory ACROSS intervals that a
                 likelihood diagonal in time cannot see. It is the price of the factorisation,
                 and nothing about the channel count makes it go away.

Both are factors with a null of 1, so they take Figure 4's palette and Figure 4's two criteria
unchanged, and both are read at theta_pool from battery_pool_G, the same anchor as Figure 4's B.

THE PRODUCT IS NOT EXACT PER PARAMETER, and the caption has to say so. Total = sample x
correlation holds exactly in log-det, and it is what makes the whole-matrix maps safe; per
parameter the reconstruction is K CDM K^T with K = H^-1/2 J_s^1/2, NOT SDM^1/2 CDM SDM^1/2, so
the diagonal of the product is not the product of the diagonals. Reading a cell of Figure 4's B
as the product of the two cells here is right to within that rotation and no further. It is close
in practice (R at N_ch 1e3: 1.024 x 1.433 = 1.468 against a total of 1.481) and it is not an
identity.

WHAT IT SHOWS. The numbers are NOT copied here any more. The `measured-table` chunk at the foot of
this file prints them from the same objects the panels draw, medians over the swept intervals at
noise label 0.1, and a note that repeats a measurement is a note that will one day disagree with
it. The hand-written copy that stood here went stale in two ways at once: it predated the
un-averaged least-squares arm, and it labelled `nonlinearsqr` LSE when that token is ILSE, so its
"LSE" rows were ILSE throughout. Checked 2026-08-11 against the generated table: every other row
of it was correct to the digit, and it was read from `m` rather than from `Dconf`, so nothing that
used it was wrong. Only the label was.

Three readings, and the first is the one this supplement exists for. Numbers below are from the
2026-08-11 render; the chunk is the authority.

  1. NR AND INR HAVE THE SAME CORRELATION PART. 16.5 / 19.5 / 21.2 / 21.2 against 16.5 / 20.7 /
     21.8 / 22.1 on k_off: the same open-loop temporal structure, as it must be, since the two
     differ by a per-sample variance term and not by anything about time. What separates them is
     the SAMPLE part, and there the split is total: NR runs 1.24, 1.02, 5.68, 47.2 and diverges,
     INR runs 1.72, 1.15, 1.02, 1.00 and converges to one. In the channel-number direction it is
     starker still, 569 against 1.00. So the divergence Figure 4 shows for NR is not a temporal
     failure at all: it is the one-interval variance being wrong by a term that grows with the
     channel count, which is exactly what the omitted N*ms is.
  2. THE RECURSION BUYS THE OTHER FACTOR AND ONLY THE OTHER FACTOR. INR to IR takes the
     correlation part from 22.1 to 1.000 and leaves the sample part where it already was (1.003
     against 1.007). R to IR is the same statement one rung lower, 1.47 to 1.00.
  3. BOTH LEAST-SQUARES ARMS ARE PER-SAMPLE HONEST AND TEMPORALLY BLIND: sample 0.92 to 1.02
     across four decades, correlation 10.7 to 14.2. The failure is entirely the factorisation,
     which is worth stating plainly because it is the concession the paper makes to the classical
     fit. AND THE INTERVAL AVERAGE BUYS THEM NOTHING IN THE TEMPORAL PART, which is new with the
     corrected roster: on k_off the correlation runs 10.68 / 13.68 / 14.18 / 14.08 for LSE against
     10.82 / 13.70 / 14.15 / 14.07 for ILSE, agreeing to better than one and a half per cent at
     every channel count, while the same step from NR to INR is the one that moves the per-sample
     factor from divergence to one. So the interval term is worth a great deal to a likelihood
     that models the gating variance and nothing at all to one that does not, which is the same
     statement 04_results.tex already makes from the ellipse areas of Figure 2.

Read together with Figure 4 the ladder becomes a 2x2 with a mechanism attached: the interval
term fixes the per-sample factor, the recursion fixes the correlation factor, and calibration
needs both.

INR IS ONE NOISE LEVEL SO FAR, so its two columns are the tiles the layout draws for a member
under `MIN_CONTOUR_LEVELS`, at noise 0.1 only. They become contours on their own once the sweep
lands. Everything else on this plane has its full staircase.

SUPERSEDES, when the numbering is settled, `figure_4_supplement_3.Rmd` (the map version of the

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
```

```{r common, include=FALSE}
# The same roster as the body figure, and for the same reason: this is Figure 4's own second
# moment taken apart, so any member missing here would be a member whose mechanism is not shown.
# ROSTER CORRECTED 2026-08-11 (Luciano): the un-averaged least-squares arm was missing and the
# remaining one was mislabelled. This file was rendered on 2026-08-02, three days before
# nonlinearsqr_g existed (added 2026-08-05, commit a202e03, which is the only directory that
# carries it), so the five-member roster was the whole roster at the time and `nonlinearsqr` was
# being labelled LSE when it is ILSE. Now identical to figure_4.Rmd:327-332, which is what the
# paragraph above requires: any member missing here is a member whose mechanism is not shown.
# LSE's cells are a staircase, 6 noise levels at N_ch 10 rising to 9 at 10^4; autodetect_cells
# handles that per algorithm and does not intersect the noise axis across members.
FIG4_ALGOS     <- c("nonlinearsqr_g", "nonlinearsqr", "macro_NR", "macro_INR",
                    "macro_R", "macro_IR")
FIG4_ALGO_LAB  <- c(nonlinearsqr_g = "LSE", nonlinearsqr = "ILSE", macro_NR = "NR",
                    macro_INR = "INR", macro_R = "R", macro_IR = "IR")
FIG4_DATA_DIRS <- c("../data/1c2ae6f", "../data/87889e6", "../data/0ffbda7", "../data/1f7138b",
                    "../data/a202e03")
source("figure_4_common.R")
source("figure_4_layout.R")
```

```{r sides}
# `stat` already carries all three components (COMPS in figure_4_common.R) with a `comp` column,
# and Figure 4 filters it to "total". Here the two halves take the two factors instead. Same
# readout as Figure 4's B, log10 of the CI-aware Dconf, so a cell means the same thing in all
# three files: the factor by which the reported second moment is wrong.
SIDES <- list(
  list(lab = "per-sample distortion", letter = "A",
       data = dplyr::filter(stat, comp == "sample"), zf = function(x) log10(x$Dconf)),
  list(lab = "temporal-correlation distortion", letter = "B",
       data = dplyr::filter(stat, comp == "corr"),   zf = function(x) log10(x$Dconf)))
```

```{r render, fig.width = 7.4, fig.height = 5.38}
# RECALIBRATED 2026-08-11 with the corrected roster. 20 columns now, 10 + 10, exactly the body
# figure's count, so the cell width is the body figure's too, x = 0.1375 per decade. The old knob
# 0.179 was measured against 18 columns and left the render 13.6 per cent tall (y = 0.1562 against
# x = 0.1375). Rescaled by the ratio: 0.179 x 0.1375 / 0.1562 = 0.1576, then one measured pass to 0.1602 for 100 per cent. Verify with
# `python3 tmp/measure_fig4.py <pdf>`, which reports iso per cent against a target of 100, and do
# not trust the nominal: the layout heights are null units, not inches.
fig4_render(SIDES, per_row = 0.1602, out = "Figure_4_S1.pdf",
            cb_title = "factor by which\nthe report is wrong")
```

```{r measured-table}
# THE TABLE THIS FILE'S HEADER USED TO CARRY BY HAND, generated instead. It went stale twice over:
# written 2026-08-02 against the five-member roster, and labelling `nonlinearsqr` LSE when that
# token is ILSE. A note that REPEATS a measurement is a note that will one day disagree with it.
#
# READ FROM `m`, NEVER FROM `Dconf`. Dconf is the CI edge toward the null
# (figure_4_data.R:199, ifelse(m > 1, pmax(1, lo), pmin(1, hi))) and collapses to exactly 1
# wherever the bootstrap interval brackets 1. That is what the MAPS want and it is the wrong
# quantity for a table of values: it reports 1.000 for every cell that merely fails to exclude 1,
# which manufactures agreement. Same trap as Dconf on a line.
#
# Rows follow the panels: EXCLUDE_ROWS drops both least-squares arms from every parameter except
# the rates, so LSE and ILSE appear on k_off alone, exactly as the figure draws them.
NOISE_LAB <- 0.1                  # the LABEL. S_tilde = label/10 = 0.01 (noise_units.R)
mt <- stat %>%
  dplyr::filter(comp %in% c("sample", "corr"), param %in% PARAM_LONG,
                as.numeric(noise) == NOISE_LAB, is.finite(m)) %>%
  dplyr::anti_join(EXCLUDE_ROWS, by = c("algo", "param")) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(comp, param, algo, Num_ch) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(med = median(m), nint = dplyr::n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(algo = factor(unname(ALGO_LAB[algo]), levels = unname(ALGO_LAB)),
                comp = factor(comp, levels = c("sample", "corr"),
                              labels = c("per-sample", "correlation"))) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(comp, param, algo)

cat("\n=== medians over the swept intervals, noise label ", NOISE_LAB,
    " (S_tilde = ", NOISE_LAB / 10, "), from m and not from Dconf ===\n", sep = "")
mt %>% dplyr::select(comp, param, algo, Num_ch, med) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = Num_ch, values_from = med, names_prefix = "N_ch_") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>% print(digits = 4, row.names = FALSE)

cat("\nintervals contributing to each median (a ragged row is coverage, not an error):\n")
mt %>% dplyr::select(comp, param, algo, Num_ch, nint) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = Num_ch, values_from = nint, names_prefix = "N_ch_") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>% print(row.names = FALSE)
```
